gate_method: gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) imported directly and run on every row via a temporary script (.scratch/checkgate.mjs, not pushed — deleted before commit) against the full draft set, using allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt. First-draft level drift (1 of 10 rows flagged on the first pass — "rope" neutral example used "tied", the past tense of "tie", which is not itself on the allow-list even though the present tense "tie"/"ties" is) was fixed by rewriting to present tense and re-verified to 10/10. A negative control (7 extra rows, each broken on one distinct axis — Latin letters in translation_he, nikud in translation_he, headword missing from its own example, an example using an off-list synonym instead of the headword, a stem with no blank marker plus the headword leaking into the stem body, a stem with no blank marker and fewer than 3 words, two near_synonym distractors leaving fewer than 4 scorable) was run through the same checker immediately after the real 10/10 pass and correctly rejected on all 7 (0/7 passed) before any row was trusted.
distractor_allowed_words_note: Distractor words were checked by hand against allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt before writing (grep -x on every candidate: crime · danger · chicken · animal · cousin · chair · sand · hill · lock · bread · cake · ball · dance · love · story · chance · mountain · beautiful · famous · dramatic · garden · wall · window · wood · music · ground · water · table · wire · string · hope · nearly · usually · quickly all confirmed present; "rubbery" — the orthographic distractor for "robbery" — was deliberately kept off-list because it is a rare adjective with no safer close-spelling alternative, and this is a manual spot-check, not a mechanical gate: gateSense itself does not check distractor words against allowedWords at all, the same open gap recorded in every manifest since 12-13/09 (C-0545 onward).
he_one_to_many_note: "roughly" (translation_he "בערך") was checked live against every existing translation_he in the bank before writing: "בערך" already covers "about" (sense 2, batch-2026-08-09.jsonl) and "around" (sense 2, batch-2026-08-11.jsonl). This is a genuine three-way Hebrew one-to-many that the two earlier rows never tagged (both carry he_one_to_many_group: null) — this row's own he_one_to_many_group now names both prior collisions for traceability, since retro-tagging the earlier two is outside this tick's scope (CONTENT does not hand-edit a prior batch file). The other 9 headwords (שוד · אדום החזה · סלע · לחמנייה · רומנטיקה · רומנטי · גג · שורש · חבל) were each grepped against every existing translation_he in the bank and confirmed to have no untagged collision.
translation_confidence_note: 1 of 10 rows is translation_confidence:"medium": "robin" ("אדום החזה", literally "red-breast") is the standard Hebrew name for the European robin but is a compound descriptive term rather than a single-word 1:1 match, carrying its own he_interference_note that a learner may truncate it to just "אדום" and lose the bird identification. This is not a guess — it is the correct, established Hebrew name for the species — the "medium" tag reflects the word choice being a compound rather than an exact single-token match, per CONTENT.md STEP 5 ("never omit a word for uncertainty").
batch_size_note: 10 rows, one sense each, full apparatus (2 examples, 3 leveled items, 4 tagged distractors) per row.
